quickStart.title: Quick Start

mitochondrial.title: Mitochondrial Channel
mitochondrial.description: Specify the channel index where mitochondrial dye is located. Usually in CZI files, the red fluorescence channel (e.g., MitoTracker) is channel 0.

target.title: Target Protein Channel
target.description: Specify the channel index where target protein is located. Usually the green fluorescence channel (e.g., GFP) is channel 2.

threshold.title: Threshold Method
threshold.otsu: Otsu: Most common, suitable for bimodal distribution images
threshold.li: Li: Suitable for low contrast images
threshold.yen: Yen: Suitable for high contrast images

visualization.title: Generate Visualization
visualization.description: Whether to generate a 4-panel visualization image containing raw images, masks, and results.

results.title: Result Metrics Explanation
results.avgIntensityDesc: Average fluorescence intensity of target protein in mitochondrial region
results.totalIntensityDesc: Total fluorescence intensity of target protein within mitochondrial region
results.pixelCountDesc: Total number of pixels in detected mitochondrial region
results.mitoAvgIntensityDesc: Average intensity of mitochondrial channel in mitochondrial region

api.title: API Documentation

q1.question: What file formats are supported?
q1.answer: Currently only Zeiss CZI format microscopy image files are supported.

q2.question: How to choose the correct channels?
q2.answer: Usually mitochondrial dye (red) is in channel 0, target protein (green) is in channel 2. You can check the specific channel configuration in the microscope software.

q3.question: How long does analysis take?
q3.answer: A single file usually completes in a few to ten seconds, depending on file size and complexity. Batch analysis time will increase accordingly.

q4.question: How to use result data?
q4.answer: Can be exported as CSV format for analysis in Excel, or exported as JSON format for further programmatic processing.
